m1.text:
Map behaviour
Click (or Enter on) a marker to select that aircraft
The entire flight is always drawn: past of the cursor bright and solid, future dim and dashed
Selecting keeps the cursor if the lane has data at that time, otherwise jumps to the lane's first or last frame
Follow keeps the map centred on the selected aircraft
The map boards and the prototype below are interactive

m2.text:
Try in the prototype
Cursor at 4:58, select T3: its lane ended at 3:40, so the cursor jumps to its last frame
Click the timeline near 0:20, then select T7 John: its lane starts at 0:57, so the cursor jumps to its first frame
Select G-CTAN at 4:58: it has data, so the cursor stays
Turn on Follow and select different aircraft

n1.text:
Avalonia mapping
Window: ExtendClientAreaToDecorations, FluentTheme dark
Frame list: ListBox/ItemsRepeater (virtualized, 144k frames)
Map: Mapsui MapControl; trail = two layers (past / future) split at the cursor time; Follow = Map.Navigator.CenterOn
Timeline: custom Control that draws a density histogram per aircraft
Selection rule: one SelectAircraft(id) in the view model, used by map markers and timeline tracks
Inspector cards: ItemsControl of Border + Grid
Instruments: small custom-drawn Controls
Panes: GridSplitter
Open: StorageProvider.OpenFilePickerAsync, plus drag and drop

n2.text:
Mock-up placeholders
Only YR-SCD's start marker and first frame time (0.026 s) use real data; every other lane extent, all trails and the mid-flight coordinates are illustrative
Graticule stands in for real basemap tiles
Timeline lane texture is illustrative: the real one is drawn from frame times
Control bars assume a raw range of -16383..16383
